findings.finding: Biosecurity Act 2011 section 107(2)–(4) preserves compatible old subsidiary rules, treating relevant import-treatment provisions as section 26 specifications. The 1976 Plants Ordinance itself was repealed; its sections 6 and 14 depend on notices/permits and its two schedules are forms/export fees, not an applicable tea specification. The missing existing specification therefore may be a saved older instrument, not necessarily a new 2011 publication. No such operative tea notice was recovered.
findings.gap: The applicable existing section 26 specification, including any compatible pre-2011 subsidiary notice saved by section 107, remains unavailable. The office-based register prevents treating online absence as proof that no specification exists.

findings.finding: Located the NPPO-filed 2011 Plant Protection Act uploaded to IPPC on 12 June 2025. Web-indexed Dhivehi text was readable; direct PDF download returned 403 and screenshot retrieval failed. A provisional reading of articles 19–22 and the definitions does not establish a finished-tea exemption; it is not an official English translation. The older English Plant Quarantine Regulation distinguishes planting material from dried/packed food, but cannot independently settle the later Act and current notice. WTO 2024 paragraph 3.101 identifies Agriculture Online System as a requirements source; its public URL redirects to a login and exposes no commodity conditions. No sign-in or account creation attempted.
findings.gap: A corroborated current manufactured-tea classification or processing exemption under the 2011 Act and December 2025 notice remains missing. The agricultural portal is not publicly readable; MFDA food-side personal-use conditions do not supply that agricultural classification.

findings.finding: Reviewed the existing precise missing-source trail. The current 324 CM Annex 5 was not recovered in prior direct, browser, Lexpol-host or government-mirror attempts. No fresh generic search or new access success is claimed in this pass.
findings.gap: The missing source is current Order 324 CM (16 March 2026), Annex 5, especially any Camellia/tea entry, processing/packaging exemption and personal-postal paperwork. The accessible reform summary is insufficient to determine whether this sencha needs special documents.

findings.finding: Retrieved the official National Trade Office PNGBA page and inspected its download links. It names the new authority but links the 1997 NAQIA Act; some displayed Act dates/titles are internally inconsistent. It supplies neither the enacted 2025 law nor a current Japanese tea specification. The 2017 draft was not substituted for enacted law.
findings.gap: The missing source is PNG Biosecurity Authority’s current commodity specification/exemption for finished Japanese Camellia sinensis tea in personal postal parcels, including whether a recipient import permit or origin phytosanitary certificate is required.

findings.finding: Reread saved regulations 23–26: preserved fruit/vegetable and dried-flower provisions are specific categories; regulation 26 depends on the Director's assessment of manufactured plant material as a serious exotic-pest carrier. Those concessions do not expressly determine Camellia tea, and no new applicable specification was recovered.
findings.gap: The missing determination is whether the Director has classified Japanese steamed/dried retail tea as permit-controlled plant material under regulation 26, or prescribed a permit/certificate-free tea condition; an applicable current commodity schedule is needed.

findings.finding: Recovered official Vatican Law LXXI of 1 October 2008. Article 3 makes Italian law subsidiary and subject to reception by the competent Vatican authority; article 12 lists particular subjects received, including post and public health. Those provisions do not clearly establish which Italian agricultural plant-health law applies to an inbound Japanese tea parcel. Existing postal/customs transit evidence does not fill that gap.
findings.gap: The applicable Vatican plant-health rule, or an actual instrument receiving the relevant Italian agricultural rules, remains unestablished. The 2008 sources-of-law statute does not itself establish automatic application of the whole Italian/EU phytosanitary regime.

note: The bounded source pass is complete; its six destination questions are not complete. All decisions are unchanged.
